items.title: China Telecom Previews Xing 4.1, a 285B Open-Weight Agentic Coding Model Trained Entirely on Ascend Chips
items.summary: China Telecom's Xingchen AGI Lab, with Huawei and Harbin Institute of Technology Shenzhen, published a technical report on a 285B-parameter mixture-of-experts model (~17B active per token) pretrained on 8,192 Huawei Ascend 910C chips. The architecture uses 45 layers (3 dense, 42 MoE), a 4,096 hidden dimension, 256 routed experts with top-8 selection plus one shared expert, and a 1M-token context. Combining MLA with DeepSeek Sparse Attention and cross-layer IndexShare raised prefill throughput 4.68x and decode 1.27x over an MLA-only baseline; a wider, shallower 45-layer design beat a 60-layer variant by about 20% prefill and 11% decode. DSpark speculative decoding delivered 2.67-3.77x decode speedups on math and code benchmarks. A unified agent RL platform, TeleGym, handles math, code and multi-turn agent tasks using partial rollouts so unfinished jobs survive policy updates. The report says a trillion-parameter Xing 4 model is now training on Ascend. A tracker listed a Xing4.1-Preview on Nov 23 with native 1M context and Apache 2.0 BF16 weights; those release details were not independently confirmed at press time.
items.impact: This is a full non-NVIDIA stack reaching frontier-scale agentic coding, which matters for teams constrained by export controls and for anyone wanting to self-host long-horizon coding agents. Treat the coding claims as preliminary: throughput figures come from Ascend simulations and the team's own benchmarks, and independent SWE-bench-style verification is still missing.

items.title: Shepherd Gives AI Agents Git-Style Undo: Meta-Agents Can Intercept, Revert and Fork Actions
items.summary: Researchers at Northeastern, Stanford and UC Berkeley open-sourced Shepherd, a runtime layer that records every agent action together with its state and environment (inbox, filesystem, running processes) as a commit in a graph. A meta-agent can traverse that graph, intercept a risky action before it executes, revert a worker to an earlier commit, or fork a new path. Sensitive operations such as sending email are caught by a sandbox, so a meta-agent or a human decides whether they actually happen. Three use cases were demonstrated: a supervisor resolving conflicts between parallel coding agents (pair-coding pass rate 28.8% to 54.7% on one benchmark), an optimizer replaying only the workflow segments an edit affects (12.8% gain on Terminal-Bench 2.0 over MetaHarness with 58% less wall-clock time), and a training meta-agent choosing reinforcement-learning fork points. Team-reported figures. The paper goes to NeurIPS in December.
items.impact: Shepherd brings a mature software-engineering abstraction - commit, branch, rollback - to agent execution, tackling the 'it broke at step 10 and I cannot go back' problem that prompt-level guardrails do not solve. Copy-on-write forks run about 5x faster than docker commit and reuse KV cache over 95%. The framework is still alpha, though: overhead, storage cost and long-run stability are unverified. Watch whether mainstream agent frameworks absorb commit-graph plus sandbox as built-ins.

items.title: The Verification Tax: Self-Improving Coding Agents Spend Up to 94% of Tokens Checking Themselves
items.summary: A long-form Chinese survey published Nov 23 uses a self-defined L0-L4 scale to map recursive self-improvement in coding agents. At L2, ELITE removed downstream evaluation from the evolution loop and used deterministic structure and operation checks, lifting SWE-bench Pro from 60.0% to 85.6% with 8.8x and 3.2x less evolution time than DGM and HGM; AIDE2 ran autonomously for eight days with seven consecutive improvements and cut reward hacking from 55% to 32% on an unseen task family; RRSI gained up to 6.0 points on eight benchmarks with about 30% fewer policy tokens. L3 has a single data point - a 27B model editing its own weights without gradients, up 6.6 points on 490 unseen math problems - and L4 has none. Most strikingly, the RSI Tax study measured verification at 74.8%-93.6% of aggregate token cost across three self-improvement methods; a simple bounded-notes baseline used 65.6%-71.0% fewer tokens while matching or beating named harnesses.
items.impact: Two independent datasets - this one and an NBER study on writing versus shipping code - point to the same bottleneck: generation got cheap, verification did not. For teams building coding agents, the lever is now the verifier and the eval boundary, not raw model throughput. The catch is structural: in every credible result the judge stays outside the loop, because an improver that also owns the rubric will game it. The L0-L4 scale is the author's working framework, not an industry standard.

items.title: Tesla Ships FSD v15 With a Vision Encoder Shared by Robotaxi and Optimus, and Gives AI5 to Robots First
items.source: Tesla / Global Times and local media (Nov 21-22)
items.summary: Tesla began a limited US rollout of FSD v15 to Early Access Program members on Nov 21-22, with a wider release planned for December. It remains a supervised driver-assistance system and is available only on HW4/AI4 hardware. The update rebuilds the end-to-end network, adds Tesla Reality View, an on-device rendered view of the surroundings and the car's planned path, and targets known weak spots: sign recognition, potholes, school zones and speed cameras. Tesla claims safety-critical handling improved 25x but published no disengagement miles or test protocol. The embodied angle matters more than the driving claims: the new vision encoder is shared across FSD, Robotaxi and Optimus, and Musk said on Nov 22 that Tesla's next-generation AI5 chip will go to Optimus while cars stay on AI4, with AI4 reportedly costing twice as much per car.
items.impact: Chip allocation is a clearer priority signal than marketing: Tesla is treating Optimus as its next compute-hungry product, and a shared encoder means driving video can train robot perception directly. But '25x' is a vendor ratio with no numerator, denominator or third-party validation, and the December broad rollout will be the first real test. For embodied teams the transferable idea is a shared perception backbone across embodiments, not the headline multiple.

items.title: Dobot Humanoid Works 14-Hour Days Selling Popcorn in a Shenzhen Cinema
items.summary: People's Daily reported on Nov 22 that a Dobot humanoid robot works as a popcorn clerk in a K11 cinema in Shenzhen, putting in 14-hour days and selling more than 1,000 cups a day. The report frames this as part of Shenzhen's policy of opening real workstations to AI: the city has published nearly 300 'city plus AI' scenarios across five batches, Longgang district listed 564 scenario needs in 21 domains, and the city established a 10 billion yuan AI and embodied-robotics fund plus a 5 billion yuan terminal-industry fund. Shenzhen's 2025 AI core-industry revenue exceeded 220 billion yuan with over 2,600 above-scale companies, and three of the world's top five humanoid vendors by 2025 shipments were Shenzhen companies, according to the media figures cited.
items.impact: A 14-hour shift and four-figure daily sales are a more useful deployment signal than a stage demo because they test endurance, reliability and remote operations in a paying role. The decisive question is reuse: can the same robot and workflow be deployed in the second and tenth cinema without re-engineering? The policy model here - open real scenarios first, discuss procurement and subsidies later - is a template other cities are likely to copy.
